authoring: synthetic teacher-style originals, not past-year JEE problems
conditions: Provisional support labels are hypotheses, not scored results
No case is scored PASS without real model admission, independent physics and claimed visualization evidence
Do not claim verified JEE actual PYQ fidelity

cases.title: Two equal positive charges, zero field versus positive potential
cases.prompt: Two stationary charges of +2 nC are located at x=-0.10 m and x=+0.10 m in vacuum. Calculate electric field vector and potential at the midpoint. Explain why zero field does not imply zero potential.
cases.independent_reference: Independent Coulomb superposition: each E opposite and equal, net E=0; V=2k(2e-9)/0.1 >0.
cases.desired_visualization: Two signed source markers, opposing E vectors, same-sign V graph
cases.risk_or_exclusion: Never replace two point charges with zero-net source.

cases.title: Dipole equatorial plane: zero potential but nonzero field
cases.prompt: A fixed +3 nC at x=+0.05 m and -3 nC at x=-0.05 m. At (0,0.20,0), find V and the complete E vector. Why is the field not zero?
cases.independent_reference: By equal distances, V=kq/r-kq/r=0. E points from positive to negative charge; compute each q(r-r_i)/|r-r_i|^3.
cases.desired_visualization: True pair geometry with potential zero locus and nonzero E glyph
cases.risk_or_exclusion: Observe true field, not a fictitious zero-field equatorial line.

cases.title: Finite charged rod on its perpendicular bisector
cases.prompt: An insulating rod of length 0.20 m along the x axis is uniformly charged with +2 nC. Find V and E at (0,0.15,0) from the midpoint. Compare finite-rod and point-charge approximations.
cases.independent_reference: Independently integrate k(lambda dx)/sqrt(x²+y²), k(lambda y dx)/(x²+y²)^(3/2) over -L/2..L/2; E_x=0 by symmetry.
cases.desired_visualization: Finite segment and actual field arrows; optional analytic vs point reference
cases.risk_or_exclusion: Rod is fixed insulating source, not induced conducting rod.

cases.title: Two coaxial oppositely charged rings
cases.prompt: Two ideal insulating rings of radius 0.10 m are centered at z=0 and z=0.30 m, with charges +5 nC and -3 nC respectively. Plot V(z) and E_z(z) from z=-0.10 to 0.45 m and locate a non-singular stationary point of V if present.
cases.independent_reference: For each ring, V=kQ/sqrt(R²+(z-z0)²), E_z=kQ(z-z0)/(R²+(z-z0)²)^(3/2); E_z=-dV/dz.
cases.desired_visualization: Coaxial source geometry and signed E/V plots
cases.candidate_engine_api: UniformRingAxisField or UniformRingField; M21b static profile
cases.risk_or_exclusion: Do not imply constrained 1D motion merely from coaxial source symmetry.

cases.title: Uniformly charged thin disc, axial potential and surface jump
cases.prompt: A nonconducting disc of radius 0.20 m carries +4 nC uniformly. Compare potential and axial E immediately above the disc with their values at z=0.05 m; describe why a single E at the ideal surface is not assigned.
cases.independent_reference: V(z)=2kQ/(sqrt(R²+z²)+|z|); E_z(z>0)=2kQ/R²[1-z/sqrt(R²+z²)]. Report the one-sided limit, not E(0).
cases.desired_visualization: Axial profile with discontinuity/undefined surface field
cases.risk_or_exclusion: Do not call the insulating disc a conducting equipotential plate.

cases.title: Grounded conducting sphere and external positive point charge
cases.prompt: A grounded metallic sphere of radius 0.10 m is approached by a fixed +1 nC charge at distance 0.30 m from its center. Find total induced charge and direction of force on the external charge.
cases.independent_reference: Kelvin image charge q'=-qR/d at r'=R²/d; conductor Q_ind=-qR/d; attractive force from image charge with correct image-charge force convention.
cases.desired_visualization: Source, sphere, induced charge distribution and force arrow
cases.candidate_engine_api: ExternalGroundedSphereBackend / analytical image charge, optional real FEMM
cases.risk_or_exclusion: Stationary equilibria only; no induced-current time evolution.

cases.title: Isolated neutral conductor versus grounded conductor
cases.prompt: A neutral isolated metallic sphere and a grounded sphere each have radius 0.10 m; a +1 nC charge is fixed 0.30 m from their centers. Compare sphere potential, induced net charge and external force.
cases.independent_reference: Kelvin image system: grounded image q'=-qR/d; neutral isolated adds central compensating image +qR/d. Q_ground=-qR/d while Q_neutral=0.
cases.desired_visualization: Two side-by-side static induced-charge/source panels
cases.risk_or_exclusion: Do not equate isolated neutral and grounded constraints.

cases.title: Central charge inside a grounded concentric conducting shell
cases.prompt: A +1 nC point charge is at the center of a conducting spherical shell with cavity radius 0.10 m and outer radius 0.12 m. Its outer surface is grounded. Find total charge on each face and E outside.
cases.independent_reference: Gauss electrostatic equilibrium yields inner face -q and grounded outer face zero; ideal exterior E=0 for the centered configuration.
cases.desired_visualization: Radial section with E and V inside/cavity/metal/outside
cases.risk_or_exclusion: Requires correct distinction between cavity field and conducting material.

cases.title: Two concentric shells under mixed net-charge constraints
cases.prompt: Two concentric spherical conducting shells have radii 0.10–0.11 m and 0.20–0.21 m. The inner shell carries +2 nC, and the outer shell is grounded. Find charge distribution and the potential difference between shells.
cases.independent_reference: Radial Gauss law: inner shell outer surface +2 nC; outer grounded shell inner face -2 nC; potential gap is integral of k(2nC)/r².
cases.desired_visualization: Radial E/V graphs and distinct conductor constraints
cases.risk_or_exclusion: Not a 3D nonconcentric conductor model.

cases.title: Two concentric shells connected by an ideal wire
cases.prompt: Two initially isolated concentric conducting shells of radii 0.10 m and 0.20 m carry +1 nC and +2 nC. They are joined by an ideal wire and settle to electrostatic equilibrium. Compare static potential and field energy before and after.
cases.independent_reference: Equal-potential final connected conductor constraint plus total charge conservation; compare exact radial electrostatic field energy (epsilon0/2) integral of E² dV.
cases.desired_visualization: Before/after fields and energy; no false time-current animation
cases.risk_or_exclusion: Do not interpret energy difference as a solved current waveform.

cases.title: Work from a uniform electric field
cases.prompt: A stationary uniform electric field of +100 V/m along x acts on a +1 nC test charge. Calculate the work of the field for displacement from x=0 to x=0.20 m and the corresponding potential change.
cases.independent_reference: Delta V=-E delta x=-20 V; W_field=qE delta x=+2e-8 J; delta U=-W_field.
cases.desired_visualization: Two endpoints, field direction, V(x) and work ledger
cases.risk_or_exclusion: Endpoint work is not a dynamic trajectory.

cases.title: Coaxial ring work with transverse uniform field
cases.prompt: A +1 nC probe is moved between the centers of two concentric-axis ring systems separated by 0.30 m; fixed ring charges are +5 nC and -3 nC, radii 0.10 m. Add a constant transverse electric field E=(0,200,0) V/m. Compare endpoint work and transverse force.
cases.independent_reference: W_field=q(V_start-V_end). Uniform transverse E contributes zero endpoint work for z-only displacement but qE_y is nonzero.
cases.desired_visualization: Ring geometry, endpoint potentials, transverse vector and work table
cases.risk_or_exclusion: A free particle is not constrained to the ring axis absent a specified guide force.

cases.title: Induced force and energy near grounded conductor
cases.prompt: Move a stationary +1 nC point charge quasi-statically from 0.35 m to 0.20 m from the center of a grounded sphere radius 0.10 m. Compare induced force, potential and external work.
cases.independent_reference: Grounded sphere induced mechanical energy U=-k q² R/[2(d²-R²)]; force F=-dU/dd (correct source-charge half-energy convention).
cases.desired_visualization: Static distance sweep and force/induced energy plot
cases.risk_or_exclusion: These are separate static equilibria; no exact time-dependent induction.

cases.title: Electrostatic energy released by connecting nested shells
cases.prompt: A pair of concentric conducting shells is initially insulated, with inner +2 nC and outer -1 nC. They are connected by an ideal wire. Compute before/after radial electrostatic energy and infer energy released.
cases.independent_reference: Charge conservation and equal-potential final constraint; independently integrate (epsilon0/2)E² across piecewise radial regions.
cases.desired_visualization: Two equilibrium states and field-energy change
cases.risk_or_exclusion: Energy released is not a simulated heat/current versus time trace.

cases.title: Electric dipole torque and energy at fixed orientations
cases.prompt: A rigid dipole of moment p=2e-9 C m is placed in E=1000 V/m. Compare the potential energies at 0°,60°,120° and torque directions at those orientations. Do not assume its rotation is already simulated.
cases.independent_reference: U=-pE cos(theta), torque magnitude pE sin(theta) with restoring direction; rigid-body rotational dynamics need an additional model.
cases.desired_visualization: Static dipole vector and angle-dependent U/torque chart
cases.candidate_engine_api: dipole field/energy primitives, standalone analytic reference
cases.risk_or_exclusion: Continuous rigid-body angular acceleration may be outside current motion engine.

cases.title: Nonrelativistic charged-particle deflection in uniform field
cases.prompt: A +1 nC, 1 microgram particle enters a region of fixed E=(0,+200,0) V/m at v=(0.20,0,0) m/s, origin (0,0,0). Determine its position, velocity and kinetic energy at t=0.10 s; inspect the curved trajectory.
cases.independent_reference: a=qE/m; r=r0+v0t+at²/2; v=v0+at. Require certified xy motion plane and genuine native saved times.
cases.desired_visualization: True-time trajectory with x,y velocity/acceleration vectors
cases.risk_or_exclusion: Clearly not an electron example; inventing relativistic speeds is forbidden.

cases.title: Velocity reversal against constant electric force
cases.prompt: A +1 nC particle of mass 2e-6 kg is initially moving along +x at 0.20 m/s in E=(-100,0,0) V/m. Find reversal time and position, and verify a typed zero-vx event.
cases.independent_reference: a_x=q E_x/m=-0.05 m/s²; t_turn=-v0/a=4 s, outside 0.7 s; a correct run should report no reversal within horizon (or extend responsibly).
cases.desired_visualization: Velocity graph with no invented reversal inside the 0.7-s horizon
cases.risk_or_exclusion: An event beyond observation duration must NOT be claimed as located.

cases.title: Particle launched on charged ring symmetry axis
cases.prompt: An insulating ring of radius 0.10 m has charge +5 nC. A +1 nC test particle with mass 1e-6 kg begins at z=0.02 m moving toward the ring center at 0.05 m/s. Study its native axial trajectory and whether a turning point occurs within 0.2 s.
cases.independent_reference: Ring E_z=kQ z/(R²+z²)^(3/2); physical a=qE/m; compare energy K+qV, and native velocity-reversal root only if within duration.
cases.desired_visualization: Axial ring apparatus, potential curve and true motion/velocity
cases.risk_or_exclusion: Do not project an off-axis launch onto ring symmetry axis.

cases.title: Classical Coulomb circular orbit for macroscopic charged beads
cases.prompt: A -1 nC test bead of mass 1e-6 kg moves in the xy plane at radius 0.20 m around a fixed +1 nC point source. Choose circular speed from Coulomb force and check one orbital period with true native motion.
cases.independent_reference: v=sqrt(k|qQ|/(mr)), T=2pi r/v; independent analytic circular trajectory; solver uses fixed source and physical xy plane.
cases.desired_visualization: Central source, orbit and force/velocity vectors over physical time
cases.risk_or_exclusion: Classical macroscopic model only; no claim of stable quantum atomic orbit.

cases.title: Two interacting charges move and deflect each other
cases.prompt: Two free finite-mass beads, +1 nC and -1 nC, are released 0.10 m apart. Animate their mutually changing forces and motion of both beads over time.
cases.independent_reference: Newton's third law with simultaneous motion of both positions; fixed-source test-particle approximation is insufficient.
cases.desired_visualization: Two moving charges and dynamically changing mutual forces
cases.risk_or_exclusion: Do not silently freeze one moving bead.

cases.title: Mass change affects flight time without changing field
cases.prompt: Re-use one verified fixed uniform E=(50,0,0) V/m and +1 nC test-particle model. Compare t to a passive x=0.08 m detector with masses 1e-6 and 2e-6 kg and otherwise identical initial conditions.
cases.independent_reference: Solve x=x0+v0 t+0.5(qE/m)t², positive root for each mass; root shift from genuine native M24a results.
cases.desired_visualization: Two trajectories and side-by-side detector time markers
cases.risk_or_exclusion: Only pair unique same-direction duration-complete detector roots.

cases.title: Structural source addition and replacement
cases.prompt: A baseline +1 nC particle in E=(80,0,0) V/m is simulated. Create a sibling adding another held +x field of 40 V/m, and a descendant replacing that newly added source with a -20 V/m field. Compare positions at identical saved physical times.
cases.independent_reference: For constant field each scenario obeys a=qΣE/m; compare only identical saved time rows, with true source replacement ID history.
cases.desired_visualization: Source inventory before/after and actual three trajectory paths
cases.risk_or_exclusion: Sources are stationary different hypotheses, not moving field sources.

cases.title: New detector on unchanged previously solved physical world
cases.prompt: After a stationary-source charged-particle trajectory is simulated, ask a new passive plane-crossing question at x=0.10 m without editing charges, mass or launch. Verify the model revision is identical.
cases.independent_reference: Genuine fresh event integration on the same source model; do not infer root from browser playback frames.
cases.desired_visualization: Same underlying source geometry with newly selected detector
cases.risk_or_exclusion: A detector beyond the horizon should remain not-found/unresolved.

cases.title: Independent sibling alternatives reuse a local source identifier
cases.prompt: Starting from the same verified baseline, branch into two alternatives both adding source ID field:aux with different E values, then remove it on only one branch. Explain why an ID retired on one branch does not poison its sibling.
cases.independent_reference: Branch-local ancestry; each child force qΣE/m independently; original source model remains immutable.
cases.desired_visualization: Fork tree with source-ID histories and per-branch motion
cases.risk_or_exclusion: Do not interpret same label as same globally shared physical source.

cases.title: Continue exploring from a previously completed fork
cases.prompt: After building and solving a first physical fork, perform a second separate call that adds another source to one of the first fork's newly admitted worlds, then ask a fresh event question. Do not reintegrate the original model.
cases.independent_reference: Actual native object identity and source ancestry across fork runs; only newly admitted worlds integrated. M35a v2 API is draft and NOT released.
cases.desired_visualization: Multi-stage exploration timeline and branch paths
cases.candidate_engine_api: M35a draft GraphWorldForkPlan v2; GraphEventInquiryPlan v2
cases.risk_or_exclusion: Do not claim released M34b can fork from a completed *prior fork*.

cases.title: Ideal charged thin shell surface E discontinuity
cases.prompt: A fixed insulating spherical shell radius 0.10 m carries +1 nC. Plot E_r and V at r=0.09,0.10,0.11 m. Does one unique radial E exist exactly on the infinitely thin charged surface?
cases.independent_reference: V=kQ/max(r,R) continuous; E=0 for r<R and kQ/r² for r>R; no single E(R) in idealized discontinuity.
cases.desired_visualization: Radial E graph with a gap at r=R, continuous V curve
cases.risk_or_exclusion: Never interpolate through an undefined surface field.

cases.title: Off-axis point beside thin charged disk
cases.prompt: A nonconducting uniformly charged disk radius 0.20 m has Q=+2 nC. Find the full E vector at (0.05,0,0.04) m, which is not on its symmetry axis.
cases.independent_reference: Independent 2D surface Coulomb integral; legacy UniformDiskAxisField is defined only on axis.
cases.desired_visualization: True off-axis disk geometry and field, or explicit unsupported marker
cases.candidate_engine_api: UniformDiskAxisField must refuse off-axis; no arbitrary disk quadrature solver claimed
cases.risk_or_exclusion: Do not reuse axial formula at nonzero transverse radius.

cases.title: Irregular 3D conductor with two off-center cavities
cases.prompt: One finite irregular conducting block contains two nonconcentric spherical cavities and a charge inside one cavity. Determine full 3D induced surface charge distribution.
cases.independent_reference: Requires genuinely 3D boundary solve and correct conductor-equilibrium constraints; 2D axisymmetric FEMM cannot silently solve.
cases.desired_visualization: 3D geometry and explicit qualified refusal when unsupported
cases.candidate_engine_api: no general 3D induced conductor solver; FEMM 5 only qualified models
cases.risk_or_exclusion: Do not replace irregular conductor with concentric spheres.

cases.title: Unpaired transverse fixed charge breaks a requested motion plane
cases.prompt: A test bead is constrained by the authoring API to the xy physical plane. A fixed +1 nC source lies at (0,0,+0.10 m), unpaired with any reflection partner. Request unconstrained free test-charge motion from the xy plane.
cases.independent_reference: Normal component of qE from off-plane point is nonzero; the declared free planar motion closure fails unless a physical constraint force is also modeled.
cases.desired_visualization: Honest unsupported / refusal with full source shown or omitted-with-metadata
cases.risk_or_exclusion: Never discard transverse force by projecting into xy plane.

cases.title: Oil drop motion with drag between biased plates
cases.prompt: A charged oil drop moves vertically between parallel plates under gravity, electric force and velocity-dependent Stokes drag. Predict transient terminal approach and collision if any.
cases.independent_reference: Equation m dv/dt=qE-mg-6pi eta r v requires a viscous drag law and boundary interaction not supplied by conservative prescribed test-charge force API.
cases.desired_visualization: Plate/drop geometry and honest missing-dynamics classification
cases.risk_or_exclusion: Do not present conservative qE+mg trajectory as the requested drag solution.
